issues.legal_issue: Commercial disposal of existing forest growth during the development of a plantation can constitute an adventure or concern in the nature of trade and make the sales taxable as business turnover.
material_facts: The assessees acquired or leased extensive forest land to develop coffee and cardamom plantations, knowing that valuable trees stood on the land and that the forest would have to be cleared in stages.
The assessees contemplated disposing of the trees while developing the land and sold the resulting firewood, timber, sleepers and charcoal.
The assessees commercially processed some of the forest growth, including sawing timber to sizes, making sleepers and converting growth into charcoal.
The assessees were business entities, and the forest clearance and disposal were part of the planned development and exploitation of the land.
issues.conclusion: The disposal of the forest produce was an adventure or concern in the nature of trade, and the disputed sales were taxable as business turnover.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(d) of the Tamil Nadu General Sales Tax Act, 1959, business includes an adventure or concern in the nature of trade and transactions connected with, incidental to or ancillary to such trade; the definition does not require a profit motive. Section 2(g) defines a dealer to include a person carrying on the business of selling goods and a casual trader. The Court approved L.N. Plantation Co. v. State, [1981] 47 STC 210, and Tamil Nadu Trading Co. v. State, [1981] 52 STC 7; it relied on State v. Burmah Shell, [1973] 31 STC 426, and District Controller of Stores v. Assistant Commercial Tax Officer, [1976] 37 STC 423, as support for taxing sales incidental to a principal business. It overruled Kuttiravin & Co. v. State, [1976] 38 STC 282, and reversed Deputy Commissioner v. Shree Shamungam Estates, [1979] 43 STC 226. Deputy Commissioner v. Palampadam Plantation, [1969] 24 STC 231, was distinguished because it turned on the specific wording of a different statute.

rule.if: sales_tax_assessment_dispute and forest_acquired_for_plantation and existing_trees_known_to_acquirer and forest_clearance_planned and forest_produce_sold_commercially

predicates.sales_tax_assessment_dispute: A dispute concerns whether sales of goods are taxable as business turnover.
predicates.forest_acquired_for_plantation: The seller acquired or leased forest land to develop a plantation.
predicates.existing_trees_known_to_acquirer: The seller knew when acquiring or leasing the land that trees stood on it.
predicates.forest_clearance_planned: The seller contemplated clearing the forest as part of developing the land.
predicates.forest_produce_sold_commercially: The seller sold forest produce, including produce that was commercially processed.

issues.definition: When a seller in a sales-tax assessment dispute acquires forest land for a plantation, knows of the existing trees, plans to clear the forest, and sells the produce commercially, those sales are taxable business turnover.

issues.legal_issue: Sales of forest produce made before a plantation begins yielding crops can be taxable when they form part of the integrated venture and are connected with or incidental to the planned plantation business.
material_facts: The plantation venture included clearing the forest and disposing of its existing growth from the outset.
The forest had to be cleared in stages, so sales occurred over time; in one instance, the plantation had not yet begun yielding crops.
The sale of forest produce was contemplated as part of the development and exploitation of the land, rather than as an unrelated, isolated realization of property.
issues.conclusion: Sales made before the plantation began yielding crops were covered by the statutory definition of business and were taxable as part of the integrated venture.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(d) of the Tamil Nadu General Sales Tax Act, 1959, includes within business transactions connected with, incidental to or ancillary to a trade, and the venture must be considered as an integral whole. A profit motive is not necessary under that definition. The Court approved Tamil Nadu Trading Co. v. State, [1981] 52 STC 7, and applied the principles of State v. Burmah Shell, [1973] 31 STC 426, and District Controller of Stores v. Assistant Commercial Tax Officer, [1976] 37 STC 423. It distinguished Deputy Commissioner v. Palampadam Plantation, [1969] 24 STC 231, because that case depended on the wording of a different statute.

rule.if: sales_tax_assessment_dispute and plantation_venture_planned and forest_produce_disposal_contemplated_from_start and sales_made_before_crops_yielded

predicates.sales_tax_assessment_dispute: A dispute concerns whether sales of goods are taxable as business turnover.
predicates.plantation_venture_planned: The seller undertook a venture to develop and operate a plantation.
predicates.forest_produce_disposal_contemplated_fro: The seller contemplated disposing of forest produce as part of the venture from its beginning.
predicates.sales_made_before_crops_yielded: The seller made forest-produce sales before the plantation began yielding crops.

issues.definition: When a plantation venture includes contemplated forest-produce disposals from the outset and sales occur before crops yield, those sales are taxable business turnover.
